record.original_question: What radiation mechanism produces the prompt gamma-ray-burst spectrum that is usually fit by the empirical Band function? The unresolved possibilities include synchrotron or jitter emission from accelerated leptons, synchrotron self-Compton emission, Comptonization of thermal or photospheric photons, and hadronic emission, and the explanation must account for observed low-energy spectral slopes, cooling behavior, and peak energies.

evidence.quote: While the origin of the external shock afterglow is relatively well modeled … the radiation mechanism of the prompt GRB emission is subject to debate.
It is difficult to identify the correct radiation mechanism with the current available data.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature through 2024 confirms that the dominant radiation mechanism producing the prompt GRB spectrum fit by the Band function remains an open and actively debated question. Reviews and recent papers describe it as "an unsolved puzzle," and no single model (synchrotron, SSC, photospheric Comptonization, or hadronic) has been shown to fit the broadband spectrum and explain low-energy slopes, cooling, and peak energies for the GRB population.

status_evidence.title: The GRB Prompt Emission: An Unsolved Puzzle
status_evidence.snippet: The radiation physics of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) remains an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The prompt emission radiation mechanism remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Shear Particle Acceleration in Structured GRB Jets (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent broad-band observations sharpened the debates regarding ... radiation mechanism. No γ-ray prompt emission spectral models, including the traditional Band function ... has succeeded so far in fitting the broadband spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, no model definitively explains the Band-function prompt spectrum.
